This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
D-30: 56, just above our 54.6% utilisation, so cells spread evenly instead of
leaving dense clusters (congestion 24,426 -> 21,635 in the rc6/rc7 A/B).
v2 (8x4, 11-12): 60. On 8x4 the cells have room to spread (utilisation 0.50-0.59);
60 keeps the core about 700 um wide with the floorplan below (v17/G0.md, failure analysis).
v2 (8x4, 11-12): timing-driven global placement. Without it the core's commit cone
spreads over ~700 um and its paths ping-pong across it (m1c: setup -0.89 ns, then the
post-GRT repair's churn congests the re-route and breaks hold); with it +2.16 ns (m1ctd).
On 6x4 (utilisation 0.69) it congested detailed routing (trial 5); 8x4 routes at 0 overflow.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds. Since v1.6 place and route and sign-off use 20 ns, the
rated maximum (50 MHz, D-5; v1.5: 30 ns, 33 MHz); the default clock stays 40 ns ==
25 MHz (info.yaml).

LibreLane 3.1.0.dev4 (the ttihp27a flow) changed the default SYNTH_STRATEGY from AREA 0 to DELAY 4; v1.2-v1.6 were synthesised with AREA 0, and DELAY 4 adds ~100,000 um2 of buffering that 6x4 cannot place.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
v1.2: 0.2 after CTS (was 0.1), then a second hold repair after global routing.
Routing takes hold slack from register-bank-to-gated-FIFO paths after the post-CTS
repair (up to 0.31 ns, through the clock feed of a FIFO's clock gate), so a post-CTS
margin alone ends with fast-corner violations: -0.106 ns at 0.2, -0.101 ns at 0.35
(with 1,100 more cells). The post-GRT repair sees the routed clock feed and fixes it
with a few dozen cells (docs/03). v1.3: its margin is 0.2 (was 0.1, which left two
fast-corner paths at -0.030 ns after detailed routing).
v2 (8x4, 11-12): 0.1 after CTS (0.2 put 2,233 hold buffers in g0x84d60 on the same
placement as 289 at 0.1) and 0.3 after global routing: at 0.2, six paths (the tripwire
clock gate, c_fflvl / c_ffmask) lost up to 0.3 ns in detailed routing and ended at
-0.098 ns fast (m1ctd); every one has >= 8.7 ns of setup slack. At 0.3: +0.200 (m1cth).
Setup margins 1 ns after placement, 2 ns after global routing (default 0.025), D-40.
v14g met timing before detailed routing, but its detours put minimum-size gates on
long wires: slow-corner slack -2.1 ns on the commit-to-pin path. The margins make the
resizer upsize such paths ahead of routing. (Latch inputs are left out of the PnR setup
checks in escapement_pnr.sdc; with them, any positive margin looped without end.)
v1.6 (20 ns): 2.5 and 3 ns. Hold repair keeps this setup margin too, so with 1 and 2 ns
it put 0.7-1 ns delay cells at the roots of paths that turned critical after routing
(v16g: -0.67 ns at 20 ns); with 2.5 and 3 ns the layout meets 20 ns (v16i).
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
================= SRAM macro integration (docs/05-TOOLCHAIN.md) =================
Recipe adapted from Loom (github.com/thomasgilbert481/tt_um_loom, Apache-2.0,
docs/tt_cmos5l_facts.md section 11) from its 512x16 macro to our 256x32 macro.
Macro views vendored from IHP-Open-PDK 2bbec755 (macro/RM_IHPSG13_1P_256x32_c2_bm_bist/README.md).
instances: key = FLATTENED instance path (tt_um_escapement.u_sram.sram).
v2 floorplan (8x4, 11-12; v17/G0.md failure analysis and floorplan screens): the tape
bottom-left, FS (pins up, towards the logic): the line unit sits by it (x 83-523), next to
the core, instead of the die's free east end, where it landed in every earlier 8x4 run
(9-12 ns of buffering on the core <-> line-unit paths). The program store, one 1024x32
(store build 1), bottom-right at x = 12 + 19 x VPITCH(67.44) = 1293.36, FS; two 512x32 or
the two-macro tree in this shape congest (GRT overflow 2,100-6,200), this routes at 0.
Macros flush to the core edge (no stranded strip); x on the stripe phase (pdn_cfg.tcl).
TT's signal pins are at the top-left (x 30-191), clear of every macro.
N/FS/FN/S keep the Metal4 power columns vertical.
lib keys name the PROCESS corner because cmos5l STA corners are nom_typ/nom_fast/nom_slow.
escapement_art: layout art, isolated Metal2 only (LEF OBS Metal1-4), at x 464.88-521.28,
between the Metal4 strap pairs ending at 463.03 and starting at 522.75 (measured, m1cth).
Both macro supplies (periphery VDD!, array VDDARRAY!) go to the single TT VPWR rail.
Full-height Metal4 stripes through the macro's same-net power columns, verified in-flow.
Magic's cmos5l tech lacks the SRAM DRC exceptions: errors inside the macro are expected.
Sign-off DRC is the precheck's KLayout SG13CMOS5L deck on the merged GDS.
D-19: skip Magic DRC entirely. It was 78-79% of each gds job and is non-blocking;
sign-off DRC is the precheck's KLayout SG13CMOS5L deck (also what Ken Pettit's walkthrough does).
Known case: POWER stripes cross the LEF Metal4 OBS in the VDD!/VDDARRAY! split band;
the GDS has no metal there (checked with gdstk). Count reported in run metrics.
IHP macros are not LVS-clean internally: abstract them during extraction.
D-23: LibreLane 3.1.0.dev3 turns an unset OPENROAD_THREADS into '-threads None'
(str(None) is truthy; librelane issue #1039), so OpenROAD ran single-threaded:
detailed routing took 4h10m of the 4h42m gds job (99.98% avg CPU).
4 = vCPUs of a public-repo GitHub runner; on a 2-vCPU runner the extra threads idle.
D-28: base.sdc with setup/hold uncertainty split (0.25 setup, 0.05 hold); the
measurement and rationale are in the SDC header. Same file for PnR and signoff.
D-40: placement and routing time each latch bank from its gate (escapement_pnr.sdc).
D-30 routing. Metal2-4 leave ONE horizontal signal layer (Metal3), and 93% of all
overflow was horizontal; at 6x4, detailed routing never converged (10-50 shorts).
Metal1 is horizontal at the Metal3 pitch and allowed by the TT precheck. With it,
global-route overflow 5,276 -> 76 and detailed routing converges in 13 iterations.
...but ONLY without decap cells. LibreLane inserts fill AFTER routing, and the decaps'
Metal1 plates (VDD/VSS) then landed under 16,701 signal wire crossings: rc11 failed
LVS with clk shorted to power. Fill cells carry Metal1 only on the rails, and every
logic cell's Metal1 is fully in its LEF (checked against the GDS, all 84 cells:
scripts/m1_fill_overlap.py and docs/06 D-30). rc13: LVS 0, DRC 0, antenna 0.
Buffer nets longer than 500 um during design repair (default 0 = never). rc13 vs rc14:
slow-corner max-slew warnings 314 -> 124, max-cap 40 -> 34, fast hold slack
+0.0007 -> +0.025 ns, still LVS/DRC/antenna 0 and precheck pass.
v2 (8x4, 11-12): 300 um after placement and after global routing (trial 6: the long
ctx-to-line-unit wires buffered ahead of routing).
v1.5: repair slew, cap and long wires again after global routing, on its wire estimates,
with 30% margins (default 10) for the detours detailed routing adds. Trial hardens v15a
(none), v15b (10%), v15c (30%): slow-corner max-slew 242 -> 26 -> 18, max-cap
34 -> 27 -> 26, fast hold +0.149 -> +0.026 -> +0.157 ns, slow-corner shortest period
26.0 -> 26.3 -> 25.9 ns; all LVS/DRC/antenna 0. Most of what is left is on the SRAM
macros' pins (docs/03).
No 2x-spacing rule on clock nets: with 1,087 clock nets (68 gated subtrees) global
routing spent 40+ minutes relaxing it net by net; at 25 MHz it buys little.
v2 (ttihp27a, 11-09): the clock tree from buf_8/4/2/1 with a buf_8 root. The shuttle's
default list met setup but left 27 shorts (lab Run 2); this list routes clean (G0 trial 3).
Row-cut halo: 50 um sideways removes the strip right of the tape (48.5 um to the core
edge); 30 um vertically gives each macro's pin side a cell-free escape channel.
v1.4: 60 um. The line unit sits between the core and the tape, and with 30 um the
tape's pin channel carried the densest routing of the die (detailed-route shorts over
the tape in v14a and v14e).
